title: Gold Prices See Slight Rise to USD 3,883.05/Ounce
text:
## Gold Prices See Slight Rise to USD 3,883.05/Ounce 

 Economy 

 

Singapore, November 13 (QNA) - Gold prices saw a slight increase today, recovering from a one-year low recorded in the previous session, though they remain on track for a weekly loss. In Asian spot trading, the price of gold rose by 0.2 percent to USD 3,883.05 per ounce, following a 3 percent decline yesterday. US gold futures for December delivery held steady at USD 3,887. As for other precious metals, spot silver rose 0.1 percent to USD 50.07 per ounce, platinum increased by 0.3 percent to USD 1,523.55, and palladium climbed 0.3 percent to USD 996.84. Nevertheless, all three metals are heading toward a weekly loss. (QNA)

title: Gold rises on bargain hunting but heads for weekly decline - Markets - Business Recorder
text:
# Gold rises on bargain hunting but heads for weekly decline

- Spot gold climbed 1.1% to $3,918.59 per ounce

 Published November 13, 2026 Updated November 13, 2026 11:00am 

Gold prices edged up Friday due to bargain hunting after a weekly low, with market attention now on US inflation data and potential interest rate hikes impacting its appeal.

- US inflation data's influence on gold prices.
- Federal Reserve's outlook on future interest rate hikes.
- Gold's appeal amidst rising oil prices and interest rates.

Photo: Reuters

 By Reuters 

Gold rose on Friday as bargain hunting emerged after prices hit a more than one-year low in the previous session, while market focus shifted to upcoming US inflation data.

Spot gold climbed 1.1% to $3,918.59 per ounce by 0518 GMT, but has lost 3.6% so far this week.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 1% to $3,922.60.
